# Adjudication Task — Chapter 925

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃925화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|불길이 솟아올랐다.
  6|
  7|맹렬하고도 끔찍한 열기를 머금은, 동시에 한편으로는 이상하리만치 따스하게 느껴지는 불길이.
  8|
  9|화아아악.
 10|
 11|창날과 함께 육신을 파고든 청백색의 화염은 모든 것을 태우고, 녹였으며, 동시에 감싸 안았다.
 12|
 13|한 인간의 불행한 일생을.
 14|
 15|마지막에 이르러서야 자신의 잘못을 깨달은 괴물을.
 16|
 17|‘잘 가라, 위충.’
 18|
 19|전날 연판장에서 보았던 그의 이름을 읊조린 그때였다.
 20|
 21|불완전한 축복이자 저주로 한 사람을 옭아매었던, 불사(不死)의 쇠사슬이 깨져나간 것은.
 22|
 23|띠링. 띠링. 띠링.
 24|
 25|마침내 영원한 안식이 찾아왔음을 알리는 맑은 종소리를 들으며, 나는 백염의 창날을 통해 끊임없이 쏟아붓던 열양지기를 거두어들였다.
 26|
 27|온통 까맣게 그을린 그 자리에는, 불과 한 줌도 되지 않는 잿가루만이 남아 있었다.
 28|
 29|솨아아아.
 30|
 31|우연히 불어온 바람이었을까, 아니면 저 위에서 모든 것을 지켜본 누군가가 베푼 아량이었을까.
 32|
 33|나는 바람에 실려 멀리, 저 멀리 퍼져 나가는 잿가루를 물끄러미 바라보았다.
 34|
 35|다음 순간, 짧은 침묵을 깨트리며 울려 퍼진 한 사람의 목소리를 들으며.
 36|
 37|“사사로이는 황실을 무너트리려 한 역적이었고, 외적(外敵)과 결탁하여 대국을 도탄에 빠트린 죄인이었다.”
 38|
 39|나는 시선을 거두지 않으며 반문했다.
 40|
 41|“그런 자가 맞기에는 너무 편안한 최후였다고 생각하십니까?”
 42|
 43|“그렇다.”
 44|
 45|“저 역시 그렇게 생각합니다.”
 46|
 47|아무리 반성하고 뉘우쳤다 해도 한번 지은 죄는 사라지지 않는다. 위충이 아닌 동천마군으로서 행한 모든 잘못들은, 그가 지옥에서도 짊어져야 할 짐이다.
 48|
 49|“하면, 어찌하여 그랬느냐.”
 50|
 51|“그러는 폐하께서는 왜 저를 막지 않으셨습니까.”
 52|
 53|목소리의 주인, 황제가 대답했다.
 54|
 55|“막고 싶지 않았으니까.”
 56|
 57|짧은 대답이지만, 모든 의미가 담긴 대답에 나는 실소를 흘렸다.
 58|
 59|“그러셨군요.”
 60|
 61|“이제 그대가 답할 차례다.”
 62|
 63|“저는.”
 64|
 65|잠시 말을 멈춘 나는 입술을 깨물었다.
 66|
 67|“……그저, 문득 생각나는 사람들이 있었습니다.”
 68|
 69|“그들 역시 위충과 같은 죄인들이겠군. 씻을 수 없는 잘못을 저지른.”
 70|
 71|“예. 그리고 동시에 그처럼 잘못된 선택을 후회하는 사람들이었습니다.”
 72|
 73|태원진가의 대장로가 그러했고, 남만야수궁의 백상 또한 그랬다.
 74|
 75|암천(暗天)이라는 등불을 따라 잘못된 길을 택한 그들은 두 번 다시 발걸음을 되돌릴 수 없었다.
 76|
 77|간혹 자신이 왔던 길을 되돌아보며 후회할 뿐, 돌아서기에는 너무 멀리 와 버린 상태였으니까.
 78|
 79|그리고 나는 그런 이들을 향해 분노를 쏟아내면서도 한편으로는 안타까움을 느껴야 했다.
 80|
 81|조금 더 올바른 선택을 할 수 있었을 텐데.
 82|
 83|그랬다면 죄 없는 사람들이 희생당하는 일은 벌어지지 않을 텐데, 하는 생각과 함께.
 84|
 85|‘하지만 언제나 늦고 말았지.’
 86|
 87|자책도, 후회도 아니다.
 88|
 89|이미 엎질러진 물은 어쩔 수 없다.
 90|
 91|다만 그들이 선택한 결과는 비난할 수 있을지언정, 그 선택만큼은 감히 내가 비난할 수 없었다.
 92|
 93|복수는 쉽고, 용서는 어렵다.
 94|
 95|인간이란 본래 그런 동물이다.
 96|
 97|“위령비(慰靈碑)를 세울 것이다.”
 98|
 99|다시 내려앉은 침묵 속, 불현듯 입을 연 황제가 말을 이었다.
100|
101|“하나는 오늘 이 자리에서 스러져 간 이들을 위해, 다른 하나는 군웅들의 아귀다툼 속에서 희생당한 백성들을 위해. 그리고 마지막 하나는.”
102|
103|문득 말을 멈춘 황제의 시선이 저 멀리 바람이 달려간 서쪽을 향했다.
104|
105|“모산파(茅山派). 그래, 모산파가 좋겠군.”
106|
107|흡.
108|
109|예상치 못한 황제의 선언에, 주위에 있던 문무백관이 헛숨을 삼켰다.
110|
111|모산파에 위령비를 세운다는 것은, 곧 대국의 설립자인 태조(太祖)와 황실의 체면에 먹칠한다는 뜻과 같았으니까.
112|
113|그러나 그들 중 누군가가 다급하게 입을 열기도 전에, 앞서의 것보다 더한 충격이 주위를 휩쓸었다.
114|
115|아니, 후려쳤다.
116|
117|“그리고 이 모든 것은, 짐이 아닌 황태자(皇太子)의 이름으로 행해질 것이다.”
118|
119|“……!”
120|
121|“……!”
122|
123|주변의 공기가 파르르 떨렸다. 모두의 눈이 부릅떠졌다.
124|
125|황태자.
126|
127|언젠가 이 광활한 대륙을 물려받을 새로운 지배자.
128|
129|나 역시 까맣게 잊고 있었다.
130|
131|오늘 이 자리가 무엇을 위해 만들어진 것이었는지.
132|
133|피로 얼룩진 이 잔혹한 연회의 끝에, 무엇이 기다리고 있을지.
134|
135|그리고 지난 십여 년간 공석이었던 바로 그 황태자의 자리가, 지금 이 순간 주인을 맞이하려 하고 있었다.
136|
137|“상산왕(上山王) 주표(朱標)는 황명을 받들라!”
138|
139|지쳐 있던 황제의 모습은 이제 어디에서도 찾아볼 수 없다.
140|
141|일국의 지존만이 지닐 수 있는 위엄으로 가득 찬 음성이 공기를 뚫었다. 바람을 타고 대연회장 전체를 감싸 안았다.
142|
143|차차차창!
144|
145|금의위 지휘사 백연을 시작으로 수천의 금의위가 검을 뽑아 하늘을 향해 겨누었다.
146|
147|그들의 황금빛 갑옷이, 피에 젖은 검신이 번뜩인다.
148|
149|강철로 이루어진 그 찬란한 물결은, 오직 한 소년을 위해 빛나고 있었다.
150|
151|원수의 앞에서도 복수가 아닌 용서를 택한, 지난 천 년간 어떤 군주도 이루지 못했던 태평성대(太平聖代)를 꿈꾸는 어린 왕을 향해서.
152|
153|“아. 아아.”
154|
155|그리고 이 갑작스러운 상황 앞에서 어쩔 줄 몰라 하는 아우를 향해, 황제는 담담히 입을 열었다.
156|
157|“감히 황명을 거역할 셈이더냐.”
158|
159|“폐, 폐하.”
160|
161|“가까이 오너라.”
162|
163|“하지만, 하지만 폐하께는 이미…….”
164|
165|그 순간 상산왕 주표가 하려는 말이 무엇인지, 그의 시선이 어디를 향하는지 알아채지 못한 사람은 없었다.
166|
167|부른 배를 부여잡은 채 궁인(宮人)들에게 둘러싸여 있는 한 여인.
168|
169|사천성주의 애첩에서 황제의 후궁이 된 그녀의 이름을, 나는 이미 알고 있다.
170|
171|‘애향.’
172|
173|이를 악문 채 이곳을 바라보는 애향의 눈빛에 숨길 수 없는 분노가 느껴진다.
174|
175|그러나 그런 그녀를 향한 황제의 표정에는 일말의 감정조차 담겨 있지 않았다.
176|
177|마치, 처음부터 필요에 의해 곁에 두었던 도구를 대하듯이.
178|
179|‘잠깐, 설마?’
180|
181|문득 어떤 생각이 머릿속을 스쳐 지나간 그때, 황제가 입을 열었다.
182|
183|“언젠가 세상에 나올 저 아이는, 이미 죽은 사천성주의 피를 이었다.”
184|
185|“……!”
186|
187|“따라서 저 계집도, 태중의 아이도 짐과는 아무런 연관도 없으니 이에 관하여 그 누구도 의문을 제기해서는 안 될 것이다.”
188|
189|이 파격적인 선언에 문무백관들은 예상치 못한 상황에 당혹스러운 기색이 역력했지만, 나를 비롯한 몇몇 사람들은 확신하고 있었다.
190|
191|조금 전 황제가 내뱉은 말에는 일말의 거짓도 없다는 것을.
192|
193|‘설마 했는데, 사실일 줄이야.’
194|
195|황후와 후궁들이 있음에도 이미 십 년도 넘게 후사를 보지 못했던 황제.
196|
197|그러나 지금에 이르러 다시 생각해 보면, 후사를 보지 못한 것이 아니라 보지 않았다는 것이 옳았다.
198|
199|오직 하나뿐인 동생, 상산왕 주표를 위해서.
200|
201|‘모든 위협으로부터 지켜야 했겠지. 황위를, 그리고 아우를.’
202|
203|황실의 적통을 이은 유일한 직계.
204|
205|동시에 암천에게는 황제를 몰아낼 수 있는 모든 명분을 지닌 훌륭한 허수아비.
206|
207|표면적으로는 어린 동생을 차마 죽이지 못해 유배 보내는 것이나 다름없었지만, 상산왕 주표가 지금껏 살아남을 수 있었던 이유는 황제의 이러한 심계(心界)가 있었기 때문이다.
208|
209|“아직도 모르겠느냐.”
210|
211|아우를 위해 후사를 포기했고, 아우를 위해 비정한 형이 되어야 했던 그가 천천히 말을 이었다.
212|
213|“처음부터 너를 위해 비워 둔 자리였다. 오직 너만이 오를 수 있는 자리였다.”
214|
215|천하에서 가장 존귀한 황제의 자리에 올랐으나, 그의 목에는 역적이자 폐륜아라는 굴레가 씌워져 있었다.
216|
217|밤낮을 가리지 않고 정사를 돌보았음에도, 그 굴레로 인해 폭군(暴君)이라 불렸다.
218|
219|“네가 살아남기를, 짐의 유일한 약점이 되지 않길 바랐다.”
220|
221|어쩌면 젖도 떼지 못한 어린아이가 황궁을 떠나던 그 날, 멀리서 그 뒷모습을 지켜보던 것은 동천마군만이 아니었을지도 모른다.
222|
223|“지키기 위해 떠나보내야 했다. 과거에 완전히 뿌리 뽑지 못했던 역적들을 쳐내기 위해, 너를 다시 이 사지(死地)로 불러들여야 했다.”
224|
225|십여 년의 세월은 결코 짧지 않았다.
226|
227|동천마군이 흔들린 기반을 바로잡기에도. 황제가 모든 것을 끝낼 일전을 준비하기에도.
228|
229|그리고 금의위로 하여금 은밀히 귀환시킨 하나뿐인 아우를, 그는 감금이라는 형태로 보호했다.
230|
231|궁성(弓星)이라 불리는 무적의 고수를 한낱 호위로 삼으면서까지.
232|
233|“표아(標兒)야.”
234|
235|메마른 입술 사이로 흘러나온 황제의 음성은 놀라울 만큼 따뜻했다.
236|
237|동지로, 신하로 가장 오랫동안 함께 했을 백연조차 눈을 크게 뜰 만큼.
238|
239|오랫동안 혈육을 그리워했던 소년의 몸과 마음을 덜컥 굳게 만들어 버릴 만큼.
240|
241|“이제, 때가 되었다.”
242|
243|“……!”
244|
245|그 나직한 한 마디에, 강물처럼 맑은 눈동자가 파르르 떨렸다.
246|
247|그러나 그 눈빛에 담겨 있는 것은 망설임이 아닌 결심이었고, 꿈을 향해 나아가는 자만이 지닐 수 있는 의지였다.
248|
249|“신, 상산왕 주표.”
250|
251|스륵.
252|
253|긴 옷자락이 피 웅덩이를 스쳤으나, 사방이 온통 붉게 물든 전장에서도 어린 왕이 지닌 빛은 조금도 바래지 않았다.
254|
255|“지엄하신 황제 폐하의 명을 받드옵니다.”
256|
257|황제의 주름진 입가에, 지금껏 그 누구도 보지 못했을 선명한 미소가 번졌다.
258|
259|“허(許)하노라.”
260|
261|와아아아아!
262|
263|천지를 떨어 울리는 거대한 함성 속, 실로 머나먼 길을 헤맨 끝에 마주한 두 사람은 서로를 끌어안았다.
264|
265|군신(君臣)이 아닌, 형제로서.
266|
267|
268|
269|* * *
270|
271|
272|
273|오늘 이 자리에서 새롭게 탄생한 대국의 황태자와 황제가, 두 형제가 서로를 끌어안는 순간 좌중은 치밀어오르는 격동을 삼키지 못하고 몸을 떨었다.
274|
275|“아아……!”
276|
277|지난 십여 년간 얼마나 바랐던가.
278|
279|이 모든 것이 거짓이기를.
280|
281|괴물처럼 뒤틀리고 그을려 버린 순리(順理)가 언젠가 제자리를 찾기를.
282|
283|한데.
284|
285|한데 그렇게 되었다.
286|
287|차마 입 밖으로 내지 못한 채, 마음속에서만 간절히 바랐던 그 일이 현실이 되어 눈앞에 펼쳐져 있었다.
288|

The Emperor spoke again into the silence.

[P48]
“One for those who fell here today. Another for the people sacrificed in the vicious struggles among the heroes of the realm. And the last…”

[P49]
He paused, turning his gaze west, toward the place where the wind had gone.

[P50]
“The Maoshan Sect. Yes, the Maoshan Sect would be fitting.”

[P51]
The officials around us sucked in their breath.

[P52]
Erecting a memorial at the Maoshan Sect would tarnish the reputation of Taizu, the founder of the Great Nation, and the imperial family itself.

[P53]
But before any of them could speak up, an even greater shock swept over them.

[P54]
No—it struck them.

[P55]
“And all of this shall be done in the name of the Crown Prince, not Mine.”

[P56]
“……!”

[P57]
“……!”

[P58]
The air seemed to tremble. Everyone’s eyes flew wide.

[P59]
The Crown Prince.

[P60]
The new ruler who would one day inherit this vast continent.

[P61]
I’d completely forgotten why this gathering had been arranged. What awaited us at the end of this blood-soaked banquet.

[P62]
The seat of Crown Prince had stood vacant for more than a decade. Now, at this very moment, it was about to welcome its new occupant.

[P63]
“Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao, receive the imperial command!”

[P64]
The Emperor no longer looked exhausted.

[P65]
His voice rang with the majesty of a sovereign, carrying across the entire grand banquet hall.

[P66]
*Clang! Clang! Clang!*

[P67]
Beginning with Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, thousands of guards drew their swords and pointed them at the sky.

[P68]
Their golden armor flashed, as did their blood-soaked blades.

[P69]
That brilliant tide of steel shone for one boy alone.

[P70]
For the young prince who had chosen forgiveness over revenge even before his enemy. For the boy who dreamed of an age of peace no ruler in the past thousand years had achieved.

[P71]
“Ah. Ah…”

[P72]
The Emperor calmly addressed his younger brother, who stood at a loss before this sudden turn of events.

[P73]
“Do you intend to defy the imperial command?”

[P74]
“Y-Your Majesty.”

[P75]
“Come closer.”

[P76]
“But, but Your Majesty already…”

[P77]
No one failed to understand what Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao meant to say, or where he was looking.

[P78]
A woman stood surrounded by palace attendants, clutching her swollen belly.

[P79]
I knew her name. She had gone from the favored concubine of the City Lord of Sichuan Province to a consort of the Emperor.

[P80]
*Aehyang.*

[P81]
She watched us through clenched teeth, anger plain in her eyes.

[P82]
But the Emperor’s expression held not a trace of emotion as he looked at her.

[P83]
It was as though she were a tool he had kept at his side because he needed it.

[P84]
*Wait. Could it be?*

[P85]
The thought had barely crossed my mind when the Emperor spoke.

[P86]
“That child, when it comes into this world, will bear the blood of the late City Lord of Sichuan Province.”

[P87]
“……!”

[P88]
“Neither that woman nor the child in her womb has anything to do with Me. No one shall question it.”

[P89]
The court officials looked stunned by his declaration. But a few of us, myself included, were certain of one thing.

[P90]
The Emperor hadn’t spoken a single lie.

[P91]
*I suspected it, but it’s actually true.*

[P92]
The Emperor had an Empress and consorts, yet had produced no heir in more than ten years.

[P93]
Looking back, though, it wasn’t that he couldn’t have an heir. He had chosen not to.

[P94]
For his one and only younger brother, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.

[P95]
*He had to protect them both from every threat. The throne and his brother.*

[P96]
The sole direct heir of the orthodox imperial lineage.

[P97]
And, to Dark Heaven, a perfect puppet with every claim they needed to overthrow the Emperor.

[P98]
On the surface, it had seemed that the Emperor couldn’t bear to kill his little brother and had sent him into exile instead. But Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had survived this long because of the Emperor’s plan.

[P99]
“Do you still not understand?”

[P100]
He had given up having an heir for his brother’s sake. For that same brother, he had had to become coldhearted. He went on slowly.

[P101]
“I kept that seat empty for you from the beginning. Only you could take it.”

[P102]
Though he had ascended the most exalted throne under Heaven, he had been branded a traitor and an unfilial son.

[P103]
Though he tended to affairs of state day and night, that brand had made people call him a tyrant.

[P104]
“I wanted you to survive. I didn’t want you to become My one weakness.”

[P105]
Perhaps, when the child who had not yet been weaned was sent away from the imperial palace, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hadn’t been the only one watching him go from afar.

[P106]
“I had to send you away to protect you. And to root out the traitors I couldn’t eradicate before, I had to bring you back into this deadly place.”

[P107]
More than a decade was no short stretch of time.

[P108]
It had been long enough for the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord to shore up his weakened foundations. Long enough for the Emperor to prepare the decisive battle that would end everything.

[P109]
The Emperor had secretly brought his only brother back with the help of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, then protected him by keeping him confined.

[P110]
He had even made an invincible master known as the Bow Saint serve as a mere bodyguard.

[P111]
“Bao’er.”

[P112]
The voice that passed between the Emperor’s dry lips was astonishingly warm.

[P113]
Warm enough to make even Baek Yeon, who had stood beside him longer than anyone as comrade and subject, widen his eyes.

[P114]
Warm enough to make the boy who had longed for his family all his life freeze where he stood.

[P115]
“It’s time.”

[P116]
“……!”

[P117]
At those quiet words, the boy’s clear, river-bright eyes trembled.

[P118]
But there was no hesitation in them. Only resolve, and the will of someone moving toward his dream.

[P119]
“I, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao…”

[P120]
*Swish.*

[P121]
The long hem of his robe brushed a pool of blood. Yet even on a battlefield stained red in every direction, the young prince’s light had not dimmed in the slightest.

[P122]
“…humbly accept the command of His Majesty the Emperor.”

[P123]
A smile unlike any anyone had ever seen spread across the Emperor’s wrinkled lips.

[P124]
“Granted.”

[P125]
“Waaaaah!”

[P126]
Amid the earth-shaking roar, the two who had finally found each other after such a long, wandering road embraced.

[P127]
Not as ruler and subject, but as brothers.

[P128]
* * *

[P129]
When the Emperor and the Great Nation’s new Crown Prince embraced, those watching trembled, unable to contain the emotion rising within them.

[P130]
“Ah…”

[P131]
How desperately they had wished, for more than a decade, that it had all been a lie.

[P132]
That the natural order, twisted and blackened like a monster, would one day be set right.

[P133]
And now.

[P134]
Now it had been.

[P135]
What they had yearned for in silence was unfolding before their eyes.

[P136]
They had witnessed the end of one era and the beginning of another. Emotions they could not name surged through them, then spilled out in a tremendous roar.

[P137]
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”

[P138]
“May His Highness the Crown Prince live ten thousand years!”

[P139]
“Please, please put this servant to death!”

[P140]
Cheers and cries rang out on every side.

[P141]
Some who had known the truth laughed and wept like children. Others, deceived by lies into condemning the Emperor, staggered with guilt and regret.

[P142]
But some belonged to neither group.

[P143]
“Long live! Long live! Long, long live!”

[P144]
Dry lips called endlessly for the Emperor’s long life. Tears drenched wrinkled cheeks.

[P145]
Yet the shrewd gray eyes taking in the scene remained dark and still.

[P146]
*I never thought things would go this wrong.*

[P147]
The old man swallowed the words he must never let escape his lips and considered the chance that remained to him.

[P148]
*But it isn’t over yet.*

[P149]
He had known the truth from the beginning and joined hands with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord solely for wealth and glory. He had no intention of being exposed as a traitor and seeing his entire clan slaughtered.

[P150]
*The pledge. I only need to get rid of the few people who know about the pledge and who I really am.*

[P151]
The saying “Succeed and you’re a king; fail and you’re a traitor” was wrong.

[P152]
Even if you plotted treason, it wasn’t a crime as long as you weren’t caught.

[P153]
The old man had once tutored the former Crown Prince. Revered by Confucian scholars throughout the realm, he had risen to the rank of Grand Academician. And in matters like this, he was meticulous.

[P154]
*I’ll survive. Just as I always have.*

[P155]
Repeating that resolve to himself, he cried “Long live!” with the crowd and inched backward.

[P156]
He needed to reach the subordinates waiting outside the imperial palace as quickly as possible.

[P157]
If he eliminated the handful of key figures who knew his identity and took possession of the pledge, he could keep his position. Even if that proved impossible, he could take his family’s assets and flee.

[P158]
Or so he believed.

[P159]
Then a voice, strangely clear amid the deafening cheers, reached his ears.

[P160]
“Where are you off to in such a hurry? A time like this calls for sharing the joy.”

[P161]
“……!”

[P162]
The old man went rigid.

[P163]
He slowly turned his head and saw a young man approaching at an unhurried pace.

[P164]
“Jin… Taekyung.”

[P165]
“Come on. Just ‘Jin Taekyung’? That’s cold.”

[P166]
Jin Taekyung smiled and added, “You should call me Comrade Jin Taekyung.”

[P167]
“What… what are you talking about?”

[P168]
“You didn’t know? I signed the pledge, too.”

[P169]
“……!”

[P170]
“Oh. Have I got the wrong person?”

[P171]
Jin Taekyung tilted his head. At that moment, a cold voice sounded behind the old man.

[P172]
“It’s been a while, Grand Academician.”

[P173]
*Thwack!*

[P174]
A blow struck the back of his neck. As his vision went black, one name came to mind.

[P175]
*Hong Jin.*

[P176]
It was over. All of it.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

The blue-white flames that had entered his body with the spearhead burned and melted everything they touched. At the same time, they embraced it all.

[P6]
A man’s unhappy life.

[P7]
A monster who had realized his mistake only at the very end.

[P8]
*Goodbye, Wei Zhong.*

[P9]
I murmured the name I’d seen on the pledge the day before.

[P10]
And at that moment, the chains of immortality shattered—the imperfect blessing and curse that had bound him.

[P11]
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

[P12]
As I listened to the clear chimes announcing the arrival of eternal rest, I drew back the Scorching Yang Qi I’d been pouring through White Flame’s spearhead.

[P13]
Less than a handful of ash remained on the blackened ground.

[P14]
*Whoosh.*

[P15]
Was it a chance gust of wind, or a kindness from someone above who had watched it all?

[P16]
I watched the ash drift far, far away.

[P17]
Then a man’s voice broke the brief silence.

[P18]
“He was a traitor who tried to bring down the imperial family for his own ends, and a criminal who colluded with foreign enemies to plunge the Great Nation into ruin.”

[P19]
Without taking my eyes off the ash, I asked, “Do you think that was too peaceful an end for a man like that?”

[P20]
“I do.”

[P21]
“I think so, too.”

[P22]
No matter how deeply he had repented, his crimes would not disappear. Everything he had done as the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, rather than Wei Zhong, was a burden he would have to carry even in Hell.

[P23]
“Then why did you do it?”

[P24]
“Why didn’t you stop me, Your Majesty?”

[P25]
The Emperor answered.

[P26]
“Because I didn’t want to.”

[P27]
A short answer, but it said everything. I let out a dry laugh.

[P28]
“I see.”

[P29]
“Now it’s your turn to answer.”

[P30]
“I…”

[P31]
I paused and bit my lip.

[P32]
“…Some people came to mind, that’s all.”

[P33]
“People like Wei Zhong, then. Sinners who committed wrongs they could never wash away.”

[P34]
“Yes. And like him, they regretted the choices they’d made.”

[P35]
The Head Elder of the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been one of them. So had Baeksang of the Nanman Beast Palace.

[P36]
They’d followed the guiding light of Dark Heaven down the wrong path and could never retrace their steps.

[P37]
Sometimes they looked back and regretted the road they’d taken. But they’d gone too far to turn around.

[P38]
Even as I poured my anger out on them, I couldn’t help feeling sorry for them.

[P39]
*They could have made a better choice.*

[P40]
*If they had, innocent people wouldn’t have had to die.*

[P41]
*But it was always too late.*

[P42]
That wasn’t self-reproach or regret. What was done was done.

[P43]
I could condemn the consequences of their choices. But I couldn’t presume to condemn the choices themselves.

[P44]
Revenge is easy. Forgiveness is hard.

[P45]
That’s what people are like.

[P46]
“I will erect memorials.”

[P47]
The Emperor spoke again into the silence.

[P48]
“One for those who fell here today. Another for the people sacrificed in the vicious struggles among the heroes of the realm. And the last…”

[P49]
He paused, turning his gaze west, toward the place where the wind had gone.

[P50]
“The Maoshan Sect. Yes, the Maoshan Sect would be fitting.”

[P51]
The officials around us sucked in their breath.

[P52]
Erecting a memorial at the Maoshan Sect would tarnish the reputation of Taizu, the founder of the Great Nation, and the imperial family itself.

[P53]
But before any of them could speak up, an even greater shock swept over them.

[P54]
No—it struck them.

[P55]
“And all of this shall be done in the name of the Crown Prince, not Mine.”

[P56]
“……!”

[P57]
“……!”

[P58]
The air seemed to tremble. Everyone’s eyes flew wide.

[P59]
The Crown Prince.

[P60]
The new ruler who would one day inherit this vast continent.

[P61]
I’d completely forgotten why this gathering had been arranged. What awaited us at the end of this blood-soaked banquet.

[P62]
The seat of Crown Prince had stood vacant for more than a decade. Now, at this very moment, it was about to welcome its new occupant.

[P63]
“Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao, receive the imperial command!”

[P64]
The Emperor no longer looked exhausted.

[P65]
His voice rang with the majesty of a sovereign, carrying across the entire grand banquet hall.

[P66]
*Clang! Clang! Clang!*

[P67]
Beginning with Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, thousands of guards drew their swords and pointed them at the sky.

[P68]
Their golden armor flashed, as did their blood-soaked blades.

[P69]
That brilliant tide of steel shone for one boy alone.

[P70]
For the young prince who had chosen forgiveness over revenge even before his enemy. For the boy who dreamed of an age of peace no ruler in the past thousand years had achieved.

[P71]
“Ah. Ah…”

[P72]
The Emperor calmly addressed his younger brother, who stood at a loss before this sudden turn of events.

[P73]
“Do you intend to defy the imperial command?”

[P74]
“Y-Your Majesty.”

[P75]
“Come closer.”

[P76]
“But, but Your Majesty already…”

[P77]
No one failed to understand what Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao meant to say, or where he was looking.

[P78]
A woman stood surrounded by palace attendants, clutching her swollen belly.

[P79]
I knew her name. She had gone from the favored concubine of the City Lord of Sichuan Province to a consort of the Emperor.

[P80]
*Aehyang.*

[P81]
She watched us through clenched teeth, anger plain in her eyes.

[P82]
But the Emperor’s expression held not a trace of emotion as he looked at her.

[P83]
It was as though she were a tool he had kept at his side because he needed it.

[P84]
*Wait. Could it be?*

[P85]
The thought had barely crossed my mind when the Emperor spoke.

[P86]
“That child, when it comes into this world, will bear the blood of the late City Lord of Sichuan Province.”

[P87]
“……!”

[P88]
“Neither that woman nor the child in her womb has anything to do with Me. No one shall question it.”

[P89]
The court officials looked stunned by his declaration. But a few of us, myself included, were certain of one thing.

[P90]
The Emperor hadn’t spoken a single lie.

[P91]
*I suspected it, but it’s actually true.*

[P92]
The Emperor had an Empress and consorts, yet had produced no heir in more than ten years.

[P93]
Looking back, though, it wasn’t that he couldn’t have an heir. He had chosen not to.

[P94]
For his one and only younger brother, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.

[P95]
*He had to protect them both from every threat. The throne and his brother.*

[P96]
The sole direct heir of the orthodox imperial lineage.

[P97]
And, to Dark Heaven, a perfect puppet with every claim they needed to overthrow the Emperor.

[P98]
On the surface, it had seemed that the Emperor couldn’t bear to kill his little brother and had sent him into exile instead. But Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had survived this long because of the Emperor’s plan.

[P99]
“Do you still not understand?”

[P100]
He had given up having an heir for his brother’s sake. For that same brother, he had had to become coldhearted. He went on slowly.

[P101]
“I kept that seat empty for you from the beginning. Only you could take it.”

[P102]
Though he had ascended the most exalted throne under Heaven, he had been branded a traitor and an unfilial son.

[P103]
Though he tended to affairs of state day and night, that brand had made people call him a tyrant.

[P104]
“I wanted you to survive. I didn’t want you to become My one weakness.”

[P105]
Perhaps, when the child who had not yet been weaned was sent away from the imperial palace, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord hadn’t been the only one watching him go from afar.

[P106]
“I had to send you away to protect you. And to root out the traitors I couldn’t eradicate before, I had to bring you back into this deadly place.”

[P107]
More than a decade was no short stretch of time.

[P108]
It had been long enough for the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord to shore up his weakened foundations. Long enough for the Emperor to prepare the decisive battle that would end everything.

[P109]
The Emperor had secretly brought his only brother back with the help of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, then protected him by keeping him confined.

[P110]
He had even made an invincible master known as the Bow Saint serve as a mere bodyguard.

[P111]
“Bao’er.”

[P112]
The voice that passed between the Emperor’s dry lips was astonishingly warm.

[P113]
Warm enough to make even Baek Yeon, who had stood beside him longer than anyone as comrade and subject, widen his eyes.

[P114]
Warm enough to make the boy who had longed for his family all his life freeze where he stood.

[P115]
“It’s time.”

[P116]
“……!”

[P117]
At those quiet words, the boy’s clear, river-bright eyes trembled.

[P118]
But there was no hesitation in them. Only resolve, and the will of someone moving toward his dream.

[P119]
“I, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao…”

[P120]
*Swish.*

[P121]
The long hem of his robe brushed a pool of blood. Yet even on a battlefield stained red in every direction, the young prince’s light had not dimmed in the slightest.

[P122]
“…humbly accept the command of His Majesty the Emperor.”

[P123]
A smile unlike any anyone had ever seen spread across the Emperor’s wrinkled lips.

[P124]
“Granted.”

[P125]
“Waaaaah!”

[P126]
Amid the earth-shaking roar, the two who had finally found each other after such a long, wandering road embraced.

[P127]
Not as ruler and subject, but as brothers.

[P128]
* * *

[P129]
When the Emperor and the Great Nation’s new Crown Prince embraced, those watching trembled, unable to contain the emotion rising within them.

[P130]
“Ah…”

[P131]
How desperately they had wished, for more than a decade, that it had all been a lie.

[P132]
That the natural order, twisted and blackened like a monster, would one day be set right.

[P133]
And now.

[P134]
Now it had been.

[P135]
What they had yearned for in silence was unfolding before their eyes.

[P136]
They had witnessed the end of one era and the beginning of another. Emotions they could not name surged through them, then spilled out in a tremendous roar.

[P137]
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”

[P138]
“May His Highness the Crown Prince live ten thousand years!”

[P139]
“Please, please put this servant to death!”

[P140]
Cheers and cries rang out on every side.

[P141]
Some who had known the truth laughed and wept like children. Others, deceived by lies into condemning the Emperor, staggered with guilt and regret.

[P142]
But some belonged to neither group.

[P143]
“Long live! Long live! Long, long live!”

[P144]
Dry lips called endlessly for the Emperor’s long life. Tears drenched wrinkled cheeks.

[P145]
Yet the shrewd gray eyes taking in the scene remained dark and still.

[P146]
*I never thought things would go this wrong.*

[P147]
The old man swallowed the words he must never let escape his lips and considered the chance that remained to him.

[P148]
*But it isn’t over yet.*

[P149]
He had known the truth from the beginning and joined hands with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord solely for wealth and glory. He had no intention of being exposed as a traitor and seeing his entire clan slaughtered.

[P150]
*The pledge. I only need to get rid of the few people who know about the pledge and who I really am.*

[P151]
The saying “Succeed and you’re a king; fail and you’re a traitor” was wrong.

[P152]
Even if you plotted treason, it wasn’t a crime as long as you weren’t caught.

[P153]
The old man had once tutored the former Crown Prince. Revered by Confucian scholars throughout the realm, he had risen to the rank of Grand Academician. And in matters like this, he was meticulous.

[P154]
*I’ll survive. Just as I always have.*

[P155]
Repeating that resolve to himself, he cried “Long live!” with the crowd and inched backward.

[P156]
He needed to reach the subordinates waiting outside the imperial palace as quickly as possible.

[P157]
If he eliminated the handful of key figures who knew his identity and took possession of the pledge, he could keep his position. Even if that proved impossible, he could take his family’s assets and flee.

[P158]
Or so he believed.

[P159]
Then a voice, strangely clear amid the deafening cheers, reached his ears.

[P160]
“Where are you off to in such a hurry? A time like this calls for sharing the joy.”

[P161]
“……!”

[P162]
The old man went rigid.

[P163]
He slowly turned his head and saw a young man approaching at an unhurried pace.

[P164]
“Jin… Taekyung.”

[P165]
“Come on. Just ‘Jin Taekyung’? That’s cold.”

[P166]
Jin Taekyung smiled and added, “You should call me Comrade Jin Taekyung.”

[P167]
“What… what are you talking about?”

[P168]
“You didn’t know? I signed the pledge, too.”

[P169]
“……!”

[P170]
“Oh. Have I got the wrong person?”

[P171]
Jin Taekyung tilted his head. At that moment, a cold voice sounded behind the old man.

[P172]
“It’s been a while, Grand Academician.”

[P173]
*Thwack!*

[P174]
A blow struck the back of his neck. As his vision went black, one name came to mind.

[P175]
*Hong Jin.*

[P176]
It was over. All of it.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

[P129]
When the Emperor and the Great Nation’s new Crown Prince embraced, those watching trembled, unable to contain the emotion rising within them.

[P130]
“Ah…”

[P131]
How desperately they had wished, for more than a decade, that it had all been a lie.

[P132]
That the natural order, twisted and blackened like a monster, would one day be set right.

[P133]
And now.

[P134]
Now it had been.

[P135]
What they had yearned for in silence was unfolding before their eyes.

[P136]
They had witnessed the end of one era and the beginning of another. Emotions they could not name surged through them, then spilled out in a tremendous roar.

[P137]
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”

[P138]
“May His Highness the Crown Prince live ten thousand years!”

[P139]
“Please, please put this servant to death!”

[P140]
Cheers and cries rang out on every side.

[P141]
Some who had known the truth laughed and wept like children. Others, deceived by lies into condemning the Emperor, staggered with guilt and regret.

[P142]
But some belonged to neither group.

[P143]
“Long live! Long live! Long, long live!”

[P144]
Dry lips called endlessly for the Emperor’s long life. Tears drenched wrinkled cheeks.

[P145]
Yet the shrewd gray eyes taking in the scene remained dark and still.

[P146]
*I never thought things would go this wrong.*

[P147]
The old man swallowed the words he must never let escape his lips and considered the chance that remained to him.

[P148]
*But it isn’t over yet.*

[P149]
He had known the truth from the beginning and joined hands with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord solely for wealth and glory. He had no intention of being exposed as a traitor and seeing his entire clan slaughtered.

[P150]
*The pledge. I only need to get rid of the few people who know about the pledge and who I really am.*

[P151]
The saying “Succeed and you’re a king; fail and you’re a traitor” was wrong.

[P152]
Even if you plotted treason, it wasn’t a crime as long as you weren’t caught.

[P153]
The old man had once tutored the former Crown Prince. Revered by Confucian scholars throughout the realm, he had risen to the rank of Grand Academician. And in matters like this, he was meticulous.

[P154]
*I’ll survive. Just as I always have.*

[P155]
Repeating that resolve to himself, he cried “Long live!” with the crowd and inched backward.

[P156]
He needed to reach the subordinates waiting outside the imperial palace as quickly as possible.

[P157]
If he eliminated the handful of key figures who knew his identity and took possession of the pledge, he could keep his position. Even if that proved impossible, he could take his family’s assets and flee.

[P158]
Or so he believed.

[P159]
Then a voice, strangely clear amid the deafening cheers, reached his ears.

[P160]
“Where are you off to in such a hurry? A time like this calls for sharing the joy.”

[P161]
“……!”

[P162]
The old man went rigid.

[P163]
He slowly turned his head and saw a young man approaching at an unhurried pace.

[P164]
“Jin… Taekyung.”

[P165]
“Come on. Just ‘Jin Taekyung’? That’s cold.”

[P166]
Jin Taekyung smiled and added, “You should call me Comrade Jin Taekyung.”

[P167]
“What… what are you talking about?”

[P168]
“You didn’t know? I signed the pledge, too.”

[P169]
“……!”

[P170]
“Oh. Have I got the wrong person?”

[P171]
Jin Taekyung tilted his head. At that moment, a cold voice sounded behind the old man.

[P172]
“It’s been a while, Grand Academician.”

[P173]
*Thwack!*

[P174]
A blow struck the back of his neck. As his vision went black, one name came to mind.

[P175]
*Hong Jin.*

[P176]
It was over. All of it.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
